root_cause.text: The vulnerability stems from the failure to initialize the stack-allocated `struct sockaddr_storage` variable in `tap_ioctl()`, allowing `netif_get_mac_address()` to leave trailing bytes containing kernel stack data unpopulated before the full structure is copied to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that `netif_get_mac_address()` only writes 6 bytes into the 16-byte `struct sockaddr_storage`, leaving `sa_data[6..13]` uninitialised, and the patch fixes this by changing `struct sockaddr_storage ss;` to `struct sockaddr_storage ss = {};` in `drivers/net/tap.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the sockaddr_storage variable to prevent undefined behavior associated with uninitialized stack memory.
intent_record.what: Modified the declaration of the local variable 'struct sockaddr_storage ss' to include zero-initialization using '{}' syntax.
intent_record.how: Ensures the stack-allocated structure is filled with zeros rather than containing undefined garbage data, preventing potential undefined behavior or information leakage if the variable is accessed before being fully populated.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is caused by using an uninitialized struct sockaddr_storage which exposes kernel stack data. Zero-initializing this variable directly addresses the root cause by ensuring all bytes are set to a known safe state before copying to userspace.

Author: Kees Cook <kees@kernel.org>

    net: core: Convert dev_set_mac_address_user() to use struct sockaddr_storage
    
    Convert callers of dev_set_mac_address_user() to use struct
    sockaddr_storage. Add sanity checks on dev->addr_len usage.
    
    Signed-off-by: Kees Cook <kees@kernel.org>
    Acked-by: Gustavo A. R. Silva <gustavoars@kernel.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20250521204619.23
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows struct sockaddr_storage ss is declared on line 926 without any initialization (no memset or ={}). On line 1003, dev_get_mac_address() is called to populate ss, but the root cause states this function may leave trailing bytes unpopulated. Then on line 1005, copy_to_user copies sizeof(ifr->ifr_hwaddr) bytes to userspace. Since ss is uninitialized stack memory and dev_get_mac_address() may not fill the entire structure, trailing bytes containing kernel stack data could be leaked to userspace. The commit adds addr_len sanity checks (lines 1021-1024) but does NOT add initialization of the sockaddr_storage variable, which is the core fix needed per the vulnerability root cause.
